url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Below is a **starter‑kit** for a modern Trucking TMS (Transportation Management System).  
It is intentionally modular so you can drop‑in replace parts, scale out, or swap languages later.  
I’ll walk you through:

| Layer | Tech | Why |
|-------|------|-----|
| **API** | **FastAPI** (Python) | Fast, async, auto‑docs, great for micro‑services |
| **DB** | **PostgreSQL** + **SQLAlchemy** | ACID, spatial extensions (PostGIS) for routing |
| **Auth** | **OAuth2 / JWT** | Secure, stateless |
| **Routing** | **OSRM / GraphHopper** (or Mapbox Directions) | Open‑source, fast |
| **Driver App** | **React‑Native** | Cross‑platform mobile |
| **Admin Dashboard** | **React** + **Material‑UI** | Rich UI, easy to extend |
| **Real‑time Tracking** | **MQTT** + **Redis** | Lightweight pub/sub |
| **Containerization** | **Docker** | Reproducible deployments |

> **TL;DR** – The code below gives you a minimal, fully‑working FastAPI backend with CRUD for vehicles, drivers, shipments, and a stub for route optimisation.  
> The front‑end skeletons are just “Hello World” pages that you can grow into real UIs.

---

## 1. Project Layout

```
tms/
├─ backend/
│  ├─ app/
│  │  ├─ main.py
│  │  ├─ models.py
│  │  ├─ schemas.py
│  │  ├─ crud.py
│  │  ├─ deps.py
│  │  ├─ routers/
│  │  │  ├─ vehicles.py
│  │  │  ├─ drivers.py
│  │  │  ├─ shipments.py
│  │  │  └─ routes.py
│  │  └─ utils/
│  │     └─ routing.py
│  ├─ alembic/          # DB migrations
│  ├─ Dockerfile
│  └─ requirements.txt
├─ frontend/
│  ├─ driver-app/
│  │  └─ App.js
│  └─ admin-dashboard/
│     └─ src/
│        └─ App.js
└─ docker-compose.yml
```

---

## 2. Backend – FastAPI

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from .routers import vehicles, drivers, shipments, routes
from .deps import get_db
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from .models import Base, engine

# Create tables on startup
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

app = FastAPI(title="Trucking TMS")

# CORS for front‑end dev
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

# Dependency injection
@app.middleware("http")
async def db_session_middleware(request, call_next):
    response = await call_next(request)
    return response

# Include routers
app.include_router(vehicles.router, prefix="/api/vehicles", tags=["vehicles"])
app.include_router(drivers.router, prefix="/api/drivers", tags=["drivers"])
app.include_router(shipments.router, prefix="/api/shipments", tags=["shipments"])
app.include_router(routes.router, prefix="/api/routes", tags=["routes"])
```

### 2.3 `app/models.py`

```python
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Float, ForeignKey, Boolean, DateTime
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship, declarative_base
from datetime import datetime

Base = declarative_base()

class Vehicle(Base):
    __tablename__ = "vehicles"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    vin = Column(String, unique=True, index=True, nullable=False)
    make = Column(String, nullable=False)
    model = Column(String, nullable=False)
    year = Column(Integer, nullable=False)
    capacity_tons = Column(Float, nullable=False)
    active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

class Driver(Base):
    __tablename__ = "drivers"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    name = Column(String, nullable=False)
    license_number = Column(String, unique=True, index=True, nullable=False)
    phone = Column(String, nullable=False)
    active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

class Shipment(Base):
    __tablename__ = "shipments"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    description = Column(String, nullable=False)
    weight_tons = Column(Float, nullable=False)
    pickup_lat = Column(Float, nullable=False)
    pickup_lon = Column(Float, nullable=False)
    delivery_lat = Column(Float, nullable=False)
    delivery_lon = Column(Float, nullable=False)
    status = Column(String, default="pending")  # pending, assigned, in_transit, delivered
    vehicle_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("vehicles.id"), nullable=True)
    driver_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("drivers.id"), nullable=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    vehicle = relationship("Vehicle", backref="shipments")
    driver = relationship("Driver", backref="shipments")
```

### 2.5 `app/deps.py`

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, Session
import os

DATABASE_URL = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/tms")

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL, pool_pre_ping=True)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)

def get_db() -> Session:
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()
```

### 2.6 `app/crud.py`

```python
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from . import models, schemas

# Vehicle CRUD
def create_vehicle(db: Session, vehicle: schemas.VehicleCreate):
    db_vehicle = models.Vehicle(**vehicle.dict())
    db.add(db_vehicle)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_vehicle)
    return db_vehicle

def get_vehicle(db: Session, vehicle_id: int):
    return db.query(models.Vehicle).filter(models.Vehicle.id == vehicle_id).first()

def list_vehicles(db: Session, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return db.query(models.Vehicle).offset(skip).limit(limit).all()

# Driver CRUD
def create_driver(db: Session, driver: schemas.DriverCreate):
    db_driver = models.Driver(**driver.dict())
    db.add(db_driver)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_driver)
    return db_driver

def get_driver(db: Session, driver_id: int):
    return db.query(models.Driver).filter(models.Driver.id == driver_id).first()

def list_drivers(db: Session, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return db.query(models.Driver).offset(skip).limit(limit).all()

# Shipment CRUD
def create_shipment(db: Session, shipment: schemas.ShipmentCreate):
    db_shipment = models.Shipment(**shipment.dict())
    db.add(db_shipment)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_shipment)
    return db_shipment

def get_shipment(db: Session, shipment_id: int):
    return db.query(models.Shipment).filter(models.Shipment.id == shipment_id).first()

def list_shipments(db: Session, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
```

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

router = APIRouter()

@router.post("/", response_model=schemas.Vehicle, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
```

#### `app/routers/routes.py`

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from .. import crud, schemas, deps, utils
from typing import List

router = APIRouter()

@router.post("/", response_model=dict)
def optimize_route(req: schemas.RouteRequest, db: Session = Depends(deps.get_db)):
    # 1️⃣ Validate vehicle & driver
    vehicle = crud.get_vehicle(db, req.vehicle_id)
    driver = crud.get_driver(db, req.driver_id)
    if not vehicle or not driver:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Vehicle or driver not found")

    # 2️⃣ Pull shipments
    shipments = []
    for sid in req.shipment_ids:
        sh = crud.get_shipment(db, sid)
        if not sh:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Shipment {sid} not found")
        shipments.append(sh)

    # 3️⃣ Build waypoints list
    waypoints = [(sh.pickup_lat, sh.pickup_lon) for sh in shipments] + \
                [(sh.delivery_lat, sh.delivery_lon) for sh in shipments]

    # 4️⃣ Call routing engine (OSRM stub)
    route = utils.routing.calculate_route(waypoints)

    # 5️⃣ Persist assignment
    for sh in shipments:
        sh.vehicle_id = vehicle.id
        sh.driver_id = driver.id
        sh.status = "assigned"
    db.commit()

    return {"route": route, "assigned_shipments": [sh.id for sh in shipments]}
```

### 2.8 Routing Utility (`app/utils/routing.py`)

```python
import httpx
from typing import List, Tuple

# Example: OSRM public demo server (replace with your own instance)
OSRM_URL = "http://router.project-osrm.org"

async def calculate_route(waypoints: List[Tuple[float, float]]) -> dict:
    """
    waypoints: [(lat, lon), ...]
    Returns OSRM JSON response.
    """
    # Build coordinates string: lon,lat;lon,lat;...
    coords = ";".join(f"{lon},{lat}" for lat, lon in waypoints)
    url = f"{OSRM_URL}/route/v1/driving/{coords}"
    params = {
        "overview": "full",
        "geometries": "geojson",
        "steps": "true",
        "annotations": "true",
    }
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
        resp = await client.get(url, params=params)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.json()
```

> **Tip** – For production you’ll want a self‑hosted OSRM/GraphHopper instance or a commercial provider (Mapbox, HERE).

## 4. Real‑Time Tracking (MQTT + Redis)

1. **Driver App** publishes its GPS coordinates to an MQTT topic (`drivers/<driver_id>/location`).  
2. **Backend Service** subscribes to that topic, stores the latest location in Redis (`driver:<id>:location`).  
3. **Admin Dashboard** can pull the latest location via a REST endpoint or WebSocket.

### 4.1 MQTT Publisher (Driver App – pseudo‑code)

```js
import mqtt from 'mqtt';

const client = mqtt.connect('mqtt://broker.hivemq.com'); // or your broker

function publishLocation(driverId, lat, lon) {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({ lat, lon, timestamp: Date.now() });
  client.publish(`drivers/${driverId}/location`, payload);
}
```

### 4.2 MQTT Subscriber (Backend – Python)

```python
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt
import redis
import json

redis_client = redis.Redis(host='redis', port=6379, db=0)

def on_connect(client, userdata, flags, rc):
    client.subscribe("drivers/+/location")

def on_message(client, userdata, msg):
    topic_parts = msg.topic.split('/')
    driver_id = topic_parts[1]
    data = json.loads(msg.payload)
    redis_client.set(f"driver:{driver_id}:location", json.dumps(data))

client = mqtt.Client()
client.on_connect = on_connect
client.on_message = on_message
client.connect("broker.hivemq.com", 1883, 60)
client.loop_start()
```

> **Tip** – For production, run the MQTT subscriber as a separate micro‑service or a Celery worker.

## 5. Security & Auth (JWT)

Add a simple OAuth2 password flow:

```python
# app/auth.py
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from jose import jwt, JWTError
from passlib.context import CryptContext

SECRET_KEY = "YOUR_SECRET_KEY"
ALGORITHM = "HS256"
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES = 30

pwd_context = CryptContext(schemes=["bcrypt"], deprecated="auto")

def verify_password(plain_password, hashed_password):
    return pwd_context.verify(plain_password, hashed_password)

def get_password_hash(password):
    return pwd_context.hash(password)

def create_access_token(data: dict, expires_delta: timedelta | None = None):
    to_encode = data.copy()
    expire = datetime.utcnow() + (expires_delta or timedelta(minutes=15))
    to_encode.update({"exp": expire})
    return jwt.encode(to_encode, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)

def decode_token(token: str):
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM])
        return payload
    except JWTError:
        return None
```
